- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is trending up, cap the rise at 2–3% above recent mean to avoid false optimism.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong upward momentum, model should not overcorrect downward in the first 5–7 days of forecast.  
- If true outcome consistently exceeds forecast by 2–5% in the first 10 days, adjust future forecasts to be 1–2% higher than model baseline.  
- When sentiment is volatile (fluctuating between 0.4–0.8) and forecast shows erratic swings, apply smoothing: average 3–5 consecutive forecast points before finalizing.  
- If forecast is consistently 3–5% below true outcome over 10+ days, increase baseline by 1–2% to account for underestimation bias.  
- For forecasts with high sentiment volatility, avoid predicting sharp reversals unless confirmed by 2+ consecutive sentiment spikes.
